rawOutput.rationale: Teach the membrane model first, then use self-explanation and repair to check understanding of selective permeability and transport.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because hydrophobic interiors block most polar or charged substances while small nonpolar molecules pass more easily.
Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.
completionEvidence: State how phospholipid structure makes membranes selectively permeable.
Correctly distinguish passive from active transport in a concrete example.

activities.label: Membrane selectivity model
activities.title: Why membranes filter molecules
activities.body: Read the model and note the two transport rules.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipid bilayers create selective permeability because hydrophobic interiors block most polar or charged substances while small nonpolar molecules pass more easily.

activities.label: Explain membrane permeability
activities.title: How the membrane controls passage
activities.body: Explain the membrane idea in your own words.
activities.concept: Explain how phospholipid structure creates selective permeability
activities.correctAnswer: The hydrophobic interior of the phospholipid bilayer blocks most polar or charged substances, so the membrane is selectively permeable and small nonpolar molecules pass more easily.
activities.feedback: A complete answer links structure to movement and mentions why some substances pass more easily than others.

activities.label: Fix the transport rule
activities.title: Passive or active movement
activities.body: Correct the missed part and answer again.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Confusing movement down a concentration gradient with energy-requiring movement against the gradient.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves down a concentration gradient without energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.
activities.feedback: If your first answer mixed them up, fix the direction and the energy requirement.

activities.label: Re-explain transport
activities.title: Transport in plain language
activities.body: Explain both transport types again from memory.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport goes down the gradient without energy, and active transport goes against the gradient using energy.
activities.feedback: This check looks for a clean, complete distinction after repair.

activities.label: Classify one membrane example
activities.title: Which transport fits best?
activities.body: Choose the best transport type for the example.
choices: A molecule moving from high concentration to low concentration without energy is passive transport.
A substance moving against its concentration gradient using cellular energy is passive transport.
A molecule moving from high concentration to low concentration using cellular energy is active transport.
A substance moving only through the membrane interior is always active transport.
activities.correctAnswer: A molecule moving from high concentration to low concentration without energy is passive transport.
activities.feedback: Passive transport moves down a gradient without energy; active transport requires energy and moves against the gradient.
